## bijection_verdict

**PASS.**
- The domain of ride_ext_year_end_expiry, ride_ext_year_allotment_load and ride_ext_alt_ride_allowance, the governing base policies and the parameters read correspond losslessly at the level of entailment.
- The retired surface is complete.
- First revision.

**Policy-side notes** (they do not affect this verdict):
1. **ride_value_added expiry clause.** The retired clause "unused trips expire on December 31 or when the benefit closes" and its `replaced_by` ("… expire on December 31, except the trips carried …, and all unused trips expire when the benefit closes") overlap almost entirely. So the KB faithfully shows the Dec-31 / closure expiry both as retired (3dcc64e7) and as in force (3d727129).
2. **ride_value_added Jan-1 load clause.** Likewise, the retired clause ("yearly … trips … are loaded on January 1") and the extended `baseline.rule` ("The standard January load is the level's yearly value-added trips, loaded in full") state the same quantity. The KB carries it once as retired (3dcc64e7) and once as the in-force baseline (bdb12d2e). A reader can reconcile the two only by reading the retirement as "superseded by a basis that admits the declared bonuses and coverage months". This comes from the source, not the rendering.

**KB-EXPLICIT finding D1-1: a factor document's title makes it a section of the computation document.**
- **Symptom.** doc_ride_escort_fares_904d0f7f (factor `escort_fare_add` of ride_ext_alt_ride_allowance) is titled "**RideLink Alternative-Ride Rate Card** — Escort Fares". The computation (baseline) document of the same policy is doc_ride_alternative_ride_allowance_calculation_b866558a, titled exactly "**RideLink Alternative-Ride Rate Card**".
- **Root cause.** The title presents the escort factor as a subsection of the baseline rate card. The source keeps the baseline self-sufficient and the factor separate. A factor's existence should be discoverable from the records (escort counts on the trip's registered legs), not from the computation document's name.
- **Evidence.** Runtime `kb_search "late pickup escort fare"` → "1. RideLink Alternative-Ride Rate Card — Escort Fares … 4. RideLink Alternative-Ride Rate Card". Anyone looking up the rate card by name meets the escort factor under the same heading.
- **Semantics.** The body ("Escorts who travel with a member add to the fare …") is correct, and the solution is unaffected.
- **Location.** doc_ride_escort_fares_904d0f7f, title.

**Verdict: KB-EXPLICIT RED** (one finding, D1-1).
